opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum grant £20,000 (New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Long-Term Research); £5,000 (Conferences, Lectures and Publications); £2,500 (Research and Travel)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating in a non-profit capacity for at least 12 months); individuals (sculpture historians, academics and conservators) for the Research and Travel category only. Not open to individuals developing their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Supports the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and funds research that expands the appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions), Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences Lectures and Publications, Long-Term Research grants, and Research and Travel grants. Applications considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation for travel and subsistence: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, rest of world up to £1,000; accommodation provided

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics or curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Visiting Research Fellowships); artists developing their practice through research (Artist Research Fellowships); established scholars for longer six-week Senior Fellowships. Fellowships at Studios & Gardens are for research on Henry Moore specifically.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the research facilities at the Henry Moore Institute in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications for 2026/27 are closed; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA dissertation and £250 cash prize for MA dissertation, plus Henry Moore Institute publications to the cover price value of £50

opportunities.eligibility_summary: BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university; dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, open to BA and MA students of all disciplines. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
